correctness.reason: Fresh integer enumeration independently reproduced 166 canonical cubic exact resonances in the stated window, 106 surviving the pair-exclusion condition, with the two claimed minimal nontrivial cubic witnesses. It also reproduced 130 quartic exact resonances and 94 non-integrable classes, including (-1,0;-9,-5,7,8). Direct substitution verifies both momentum and divisor equations, and the infinite P(l)=0 family follows algebraically from L^3-L being divisible by 6.
risks: Only the zero-amplitude linear divisor is certified; finite-amplitude detuning is outside the claim.

originality.reason: Kappeler–Montalto provide the published Melnikov framework and explicitly identify momentum-preserving perturbations as a route toward longer stability, but the inspected paper does not supply these exact momentum-preserving zero-divisor tuples or the bounded census. Exact tuple searches and the mathematical-record search found no prior covering statement.
risks: Other normal-form papers may contain equivalent low-order resonance classifications under different notation; none was located in the targeted searches.

value.reason: The witnesses test a natural published route: imposing momentum conservation does not eliminate all linear exact resonances relevant to the next normal-form step. The cubic and quartic obstructions are small, hand-checkable, and paired with exhaustive bounded counts, so they are motivated structural boundary data rather than an arbitrary finite table.
risks: They do not prove failure of finite-amplitude long-time stability; significance is limited to the linear divisor obstruction.

broader_coverage: Kappeler–Montalto supply the normal-form/Melnikov framework and motivate momentum preservation, but do not classify these exact S+={1,2} resonances.
